# Minimum rates you must pay workers

The minimum pay rates providers must pass on to eligible workers to meet worker retention payment conditions.

## On this page:

## About this page

This page provides a simple guide to the rates you must pay eligible workers if you receive the worker retention payment. It contains the rates you **currently** need to pay workers to meet conditions. These rates apply from 1 July 2026.

For more detailed information, including how rates are calculated and applied, refer to the grant guidelines. The guidelines contain additional information about:

- classification levels
- award coverage
- rate calculations
- transition arrangements
- Annual Wage Review interactions
- historical rates.

All grantees **must** read and become familiar with the grant guidelines.

[Go to the worker retention payment guidelines](https://www.grants.gov.au/Go/Show?GoUuid=99ae5ad1-d749-4a9c-8fdc-72259be9469d)

## How to use this page

1\. **Choose the award that covers the worker**

Use the table that applies to the worker:

- [Children's Services Award 2010 – workers engaged on or before 28 February 2026](https://www.education.gov.au/early-childhood/providers/workforce/worker-retention-payment/minimum-rates#toc-children-s-services-award-2010-workers-engaged-on-or-before-28-february-2026)
- [Children's Services Award 2010 – workers engaged on or after 1 March 2026](https://www.education.gov.au/early-childhood/providers/workforce/worker-retention-payment/minimum-rates#toc-children-s-services-award-2010-workers-engaged-on-or-after-1-march-2026)
- [Educational Services (Teachers) Award 2020](https://www.education.gov.au/early-childhood/providers/workforce/worker-retention-payment/minimum-rates#toc-educational-services-teachers-award-2020)

**2\. Find the worker’s classification**

**3\. Check the minimum hourly rate**

Use the **minimum hourly rate column** to check the total minimum hourly rate the worker must be paid.

**4\. Check the WRP contribution**

Use one of the **WRP contribution columns** to check the minimum amount of grant funding that must be passed on as wages. Use the:

- **standard amount column** for workers whose hourly rate on 30 June 2026 was **below** the new minimum hourly rate from 1 July 2026
- **already paying minimum hourly rate column** for workers whose hourly rate on 30 June 2026 was **at or above** the new minimum hourly rate from 1 July 2026.

The same approach also applies to eligible casual workers. Use the lower amount if the worker's hourly rate on 30 June 2026 was at or above the applicable minimum WRP casual rate from 1 July 2026. Otherwise, use the standard amount. You must also use one of the 2 calculation methods outlined in the grant guidelines.

Check the previous hourly rates in the [grant guidelines](https://www.grants.gov.au/Go/Show?GoUuid=99ae5ad1-d749-4a9c-8fdc-72259be9469d).

**Do I need to add the WRP contribution to the minimum hourly rate?**

You must pay each eligible worker at least the minimum hourly rate and pass on the required WRP contribution.

The WRP contribution can count towards the minimum hourly rate, provided it is not used to subsidise your existing wages (except as outlined in section 5.3 of the [grant guidelines](https://www.grants.gov.au/Go/Show?GoUuid=99ae5ad1-d749-4a9c-8fdc-72259be9469d)).

If you already pay a worker above the minimum hourly rate, you may need to further increase their wages to ensure the required WRP contribution is passed on. Refer to the grant guidelines for certainty.

**Why are there two WRP contribution columns?**

Workers who were already being paid at or above the applicable minimum hourly rate before 1 July 2026 are not entitled to a pay increase as a result of the Annual Wage Review. In these cases, the WRP contribution amount may remain unchanged.

## Rates prior to 1 July 2026

This page contains the current minimum rates that apply from 1 July 2026. For rates that applied before 1 July 2026, refer to the [grant guidelines](https://www.grants.gov.au/Go/Show?GoUuid=99ae5ad1-d749-4a9c-8fdc-72259be9469d).

## Examples to help you understand

These examples illustrate different scenarios for correctly paying workers where Table 14 in the current grant guidelines applies, including when to use Column 5 or Column 6.

### Example 1: Worker paid below the new minimum WRP hourly rate

Jane is a Level 3 – Qualified Educator covered by the Children's Services Award 2010 who was engaged on or after 1 March 2026.

On 30 June 2026, Jane’s employer was a WRP grantee and paid Jane $32.34 per hour (inclusive of the WRP contribution). This was the minimum WRP hourly rate that applied at that time.

From 1 July 2026, the minimum WRP hourly rate increased to $33.87 per hour.

To continue meeting the grant conditions from 1 July 2026, the grantee was required to:

- increase Jane’s total rate of pay to at least $33.87 per hour, and
- pass on at least $4.42 per hour of grant funding as wages, noting this amount can form part of the $33.87 hourly rate.

The WRP contribution (standard amount) in Column 5 of Table 14 applies because Jane's hourly rate on 30 June 2026 was lower than the minimum hourly rate that applied from 1 July 2026.

The standard WRP contribution also applies to workers who were paid above the old minimum WRP rate, but below the new minimum WRP rate.

### Example 2: Worker already paid above the new minimum WRP hourly rate

Steve is a Level 3 – Qualified Educator covered by the Children's Services Award 2010 who was engaged on or after 1 March 2026.

On 30 June 2026, Steve’s employer was a WRP grantee and paid Steve $35.00 per hour (inclusive of WRP contribution), which is above the minimum WRP hourly rate of $32.34 that applied at the time.

From 1 July 2026, the minimum WRP hourly rate increased to $33.87 per hour. Because Steve was already being paid more than this amount, he is not entitled to a pay increase.

To continue meeting the grant conditions from 1 July 2026, the grantee was required to:

- continue to pay Steve a total rate of at least $35.00 per hour, and
- continue to pass on at least $4.22 per hour of grant funding as wages, noting this amount can form part of the $35.00 hourly rate.

The WRP contribution (already paying minimum hourly rate) in Column 6 of Table 14  applies because Steve's hourly rate on 30 June 2026 was already above the minimum WRP rate that applied from 1 July 2026.

## Rate changes

Rates may change due to:

- an [annual wage review](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/workplace-laws/annual-wage-review) by the Fair Work Commission
- outcomes of the [gender-based undervaluation priority awards review](https://www.fwc.gov.au/hearings-decisions/major-cases/gender-undervaluation-priority-awards-review).
